prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: 1. Everyone has the right freely to participate in the cultural life of the community, to enjoy the arts and to share in scientific advancement and its benefits.
DEMAND: Everyone has the right freely to participate in the cultural life of the community, to enjoy the arts and to share in scientific advancement and its benefits
BEARER: everyone

cli.result:
1. Everyone may freely take part in the cultural life of the community. Separately, everyone may enjoy the arts and may share in scientific advancement and its benefits. Here "freely" applies only to taking part in cultural life.
2. Everyone may freely take part in the cultural life of the community, freely enjoy the arts, and freely share in scientific advancement and its benefits. Here "freely" applies to all three acts, and each is a separate right.
3. Everyone may share in scientific advancement itself, such as taking part in it, and may separately share in its benefits. These are two distinct rights alongside the right to take part in cultural life and the right to enjoy the arts.
